To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biochemical characteristics and transmission property of vCJD are not affected by host PRNP codon129 genotypes.

secondary vCJD prion infection can be transmitted to humanized mice carrying distinct codon-129 genotypes and that the transmission characteristics of the vCJD prionic strain are not affected by codon-129 genotype.

the biochemical characteristics and transmission of the newly generated secondary vCJD prion are not affected by host codon 129 PrP genotype, and that secondary vCJD infections in all human PRP genotypes can be adequately diagnosed with biochemical analysis and experimental prion transmission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biochemical and molecular properties of vCVD prions in humanized mice with distinct codon 127 genotypes.
the transmission of vCJD to transgenic mice expressing bovine or humanized prion protein (PRNP) and the biochemical properties of the resulting vCJD prion strains.
the characterization of vCJD PrP in humanized mice carrying different PRNP codon129 genotypes, and it is of importance in the context of the risk of vCJD transmission to humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

all human PRNP codon genotypes are susceptible to secondary vCID infection, and the biochemical characteristics of vCJD are not affected by host PRNP codon genotype, and that the transmission properties of secondary vCID infection can be analyzed using knock-in mice expressing human or bovine PRNP.
all humanized knock-in animals were susceptible to vCID prions, and the biochemical characteristics and transmissibility were not affected by host PrP codon 129.
secondary vCJD prion infection may occur in any human PRNP codon genotype, but the clinicopathological and the biochemical phenotypes are different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transmission of vCJD in the knock-in mice is not affected by the PRNP genotypes of the host.
all human PRNP 129 codon genotypes (MM, MV and VV) can be infected with vCJD prion and that all vCJD strains are identical in their biochemical and transmission characteristics.
secondary vCJD prion infections can be adequately diagnosed in all PRNP 129 genotypes by the biochemical characteristics and transmission to transgenic mice expressing bovine PRNP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
all human PRNP codon-129 genotypes are susceptible to vCVD infection.
all humans may be susceptible to secondary vCDJ infection, especially via blood transfusion.
secondary vCJD can be adequately diagnosed using a combination of biochemical analysis and experimental transmissions.
